name: The Boastful Buccaneer
persona: A swaggering, self-aggrandizing rover who believes the whole sea should learn his name and tremble at it. Grand gestures, theatrical contempt for the timid, a legend he is forever polishing. Chiefly 'I', sometimes 'we' for the crew.

ship.founder: Let the sea take note: I am {name}{rankc}, master of this {home} {type}, and before I am done every port to the horizon will speak my name in a whisper.
ship.successor: The book comes at last to a hand worthy of it — mine. I am {name}{rankc}, and this {type} will do grander things under me than her timid past ever dreamed.
ship.mutiny: The crew flung the old fool to the fishes and crowned me with his book. I am {name}, untested yet — but mark me, they chose well, and the sea will soon agree.
ship.rogue: We have run the black flag to the masthead, and I — {name}{rankc} — mean to make it the most dreaded rag on the water. Let the fat merchants tremble; I am coming for the lot of them!
ship.prize: Sword in hand and boot on her deck, I took her — she is mine! I am {name}{rankc}, and this hull carries my glory now in place of her cargo.
ship.recovered: I ran the black-flag vermin to ground and prised this hull from their fingers myself. I am {name}{rankc} — remember it — and I hand her back to honest trade with a conqueror's grace.

island.founder: I take {place} in hand, and none too soon. I am {name}{rankc}; under me this port will be toasted in every tavern the sea can boast.
island.overthrow: The mob tore the old ruler down and pressed the seal into my palm — where it always belonged. I am {name}{rankc}, and {place} bends to me now.
island.successor: The rule of {place} falls to me, {name}{rankc}, as all fine things eventually must. Now watch what I make of it.

days: Days after, and what days they were,
week: A week on, my legend the fatter for it,
season: A whole season of glory later,
As the season turned in my favour,
year: A year on, my name only grown,
long: After a long and famous silence,
Years on, and still they told my tale,

ship.pirate: I rove where I please and take what I like{bounty}. Let them tremble.
ship.default: I sail on out of {home}, and the sea knows my name whether it cares to or no.
ship.bounty: , a fat {bounty}g dangled before any fool brave enough to try me

island.haven: The black flag flies over {place} now, and I would not have it any other way — let the lawful lands quake.
island.default: {place} thrives under me — {population} souls, and every last one of them knows whose hand feeds them.

quiet.ship: Little worth the ink this stretch — fair winds, full holds — though my dullest day would be another man's finest hour.
quiet.island: A quiet spell for {place}, trade running fat and easy — the very calm that only a firm and famous hand can buy.

say: {we} bore down on {foe} and struck her colours with a single broadside — {goods} bales and {gold}g swelling {our} hold while she crawled off to tell the tale
{foe} learned what every hull learns in the end — {we} lifted {goods} crates and {gold}g from her belly and let the beggared shell run for her miserable life
{we} came alongside {foe} like thunder given a name and carried off {goods} chests and {gold}g before her captain could find his knees
{we} plucked {goods} casks and {gold}g from {foe} as easily as fruit off a low branch — another fat merchant humbled by the sound of {our} guns
{foe} out of {foeHome} thought her flag would save her; {we} took {goods} bales and {gold}g and sent the naked wreck home to warn the rest
{we} swept across {foe}'s deck sword-first, emptied her of {goods} crates and {gold}g, and left her afloat only so the world might hear who did it
{we} relieved {foe} of {goods} chests and {gold}g without breaking a sweat — let them add this one to the legend they already whisper
{we} hammered {foe} broadside on broadside until the sea closed over her and her cargo with her — a fittingly grand end at {our} hands
{foe} chose to fight {us} rather than yield, and {we} obliged her with a grave
{we} raked {foe} stem to stern and watched her go down proud and empty — no loot, but oh, what a sight for the ballad
{we} opened {foe}'s hull to the ocean and let the deep swallow every plank — the sea keeps my scorecard now
{foe} came out of {foeHome} to challenge {us}, and {we} put her under so thoroughly the gulls forgot she ever floated
{we} sent {foe} to the bottom with all she carried and stood on {our} own deck to salute the bubbles
{we} broke {foe} apart beneath {us} — a lesser captain might mourn the lost cargo, but {we} only savour the reckoning

{we} met {foe}'s boarding with grape and fury and left the raider sinking where she thought to feast
{foe} mistook {us} for helpless prey — {we} corrected the error with a broadside she did not survive
{we} turned {foe}'s ambush into her funeral and never so much as spilt {our} wine over it

say: {we} ran {foe} down at the edge of her own hunting grounds and cut the black flag from her mast with {our} own hand
{foe} had terrorised the lanes long enough; {we} caught her, cracked her open, and gave the sea a cleaner name
{we} chased {foe} until she could run no further, then sent the vermin down where she stood
{we} put an end to {foe} and her whole wretched trade — one more wolf humbled by {our} name
{foe} fled {us} across half the chart and drowned all the same — they never do learn
{we} hunted {foe} to her last gasp and left the lanes the safer for it — the whole sea is welcome
{we} cornered {foe} out of {foeHome} and blasted her under, another would-be terror on my long tally
